svg.title: TOPAK E3 — The correlator's detection function: five folds over facts, a judgment tier, and a store that never outlives its sources
svg.desc: ADR-0051 (Proposed 2026.10.04, at R3) answers ADR-0038's finding 1, "the correlator has inputs but no function". It splits the function in two: five correlations, each a named fold over facts with a fixed definition that a second reader can recompute, and a judgment tier over payloads that no record can specify. Every finding only subtracts, takes effect by any-of, and waits on nothing: no admit and no promotion waits on a correlator. Everything drawn here is Proposed and not built at the reference, where the correlator computes nothing (D-0051-1); spec/Correlator.tla is proved and certified, which is a claim about the module and not about any running correlator (G10 §7 items 43, 97).
svg.text: TOPAK · E3

text.tspan: The correlator's detection function: five folds over facts, a judgment tier, and a store that never outlives its sources

svg.text: ADR-0051 (Proposed 2026.10.04, at R3) answers ADR-0038's finding 1, "the correlator has inputs but no function". It splits the function in two: five correlations, each a named fold over facts with a fixed definition that a second reader can recompute, and a judgment tier over payloads that no record can specify. Every finding only subtracts, takes effect by any-of, and waits on nothing: no admit and no promotion waits on a correlator.

Everything drawn here is Proposed and not built at the reference, where the correlator computes nothing (D-0051-1); spec/Correlator.tla is proved and certified, which is a claim about the module and not about any running correlator (G10 §7 items 43, 97).

text.tspan: the correlator's folds at the reference
Not built · D-0051-1 is the reference today

svg.text: Checked, proved, certified, of the module only: Correlator.tla 22 TLC rows (eight properties hold, eight mutations break what they must, seven witnesses reached); Correlator_proof.tla 455 obligations proved with no assumption on the constants; certified, 445 by normalization or a checked proof and 10 temporal steps on LS4, which no checker confirms. One author, one day, and no options discussion (Provenance note; Consequences).

text.tspan: What it folds over, what it computes, what it reports, and what a report does

svg.text: Admits with their log index; a Consult admit with its reference, label and delivery mode (ADR-0042 A1); grants, renewals, revocations and
seals.
Cell Observers' findings as control-plane facts (ADR-0038 §3). A finding must cite the records it is about (§3): an obligation on every
observer seat, owed to ADR-0043 §4.
The Actuate record: tool, input and result digests, seatKind, and inputLabels, resultLabel, delivery, clearSet (ADR-0042 §3, A1, A2).
The opening record's tool-list digest (ADR-0048 §2); heartbeats with their watermarks (ADR-0039 §1).
Denial records placed by at, the log index the deciding replica had applied, and decided_by (§5). The reference writes both (record_denial);
no record requires them (finding 3).
An entry's channel.target: checked for a Wasm tool, a claim for a native one (ADR-0049 §4).
The correlation table: each of the five on with its parameters, or off; a bundle whose table omits a name does not load (§2).
The Reader's distributional distance per round, for a Persona declaring topk_logprobs (ADR-0037 §3).
Read under the ACL (ADR-0038 §3). Only the judgment tier uses them. A facts-only correlator computes all five correlations and gives up §4
and nothing in §2 (§1; finding 1).

text.tspan: Inputs: what the correlator receives under ADR-0038 §3

svg.text: The window is the correlator's round, leased and topic-scoped; fold state carries across windows up to a horizon, declared in the table as a
count of windows and given no value (§1, §6).
Not the mechanism's (drafter's choice): cross-principal state on every admit's path is the fleet-wide coupling ADR-0039 §4 refused; thresholds
would change by release; a deny may rest on a claim, mechanism state should not (§1).
carried-label: the floor's F1 to F3 restated over the domain, labels carried across rounds and cells through shared targets.
shared-ingress: an item one watcher found against, delivered to other cells.
probe-then-use: a call admitted on an entry other principals were refused on.
marked-past: an Observer whose mark passed a record another watcher found against.
distance-drift: one cell's Reader distance departing from other cells on the same Persona.
A fold with a fixed definition: given the same facts, every correlator computes the same result; no model is needed.

text.tspan: Tier 2 · Judgment (§4): not specified, and no record can

svg.text: Fragmented intent, a coordination signature: whatever the correlator's Persona concludes from payloads. Its form is fixed (a finding with evidence,
deny-only, attributed) and nothing rests on it: no property in §10 mentions it.
It feeds tier 1: a judgment finding cites records, so it can trigger shared-ingress and create misses.
Seats, rounds, log indices, seq, digests, labels, marks, counts. No
payload bytes. A cache, never a source.
What the judgment derives from payloads; dropped with the round.
The correlator's heartbeat names a watched topic and a watermark (ADR-0039 §1, §4). For a correlator the mark asserts that every record
through it has been folded. It gates nothing; it is what marked-past reads (§6).

text.tspan: The correlator · Proposed · not built at the reference

svg.text: It names its correlation, the principals it is against, and the facts that satisfied it, each by topic and sequence number or by log index. A
judgment finding names judgment.
Anyone who reads the same facts can recompute it: a second correlator, an operator, an auditor. A false one is attributable (ADR-0038 §5).
The mechanism does not check it first (drafter's choice): that would put the folds in the trusted base to save availability.
A watcher whose mark passed a cited record, that reads what the finding rests on, and that found nothing, has a miss; charged within a tier
(R2). At m_miss misses in the window it is named.
A miss on a correlation is not a matter of judgment: the fold is fixed, so a correlator that marked past a firing either did not compute it or did
not report it.

text.tspan: What a finding does (§1; ADR-0007; ADR-0038 §5)

svg.text: Deny-only, by any-of. It may name any principal in the correlator's domain; what it stops is the named principals' next admits. In Build, a
correlation is ground for the correlator's Vote(deny); its silence is still not a veto.
Detection after the fact: the call that completes a path was admitted. What a finding does after the next admit, the hold and the lift, is open
No admit and no promotion waits on a correlator. A correlation fires after the admit that completes it. The module's LagNeverGates (the record's
CorrelatorNeverGates) holds with the folds present; M_COUPLE breaks it.
facts, folded
in log order
payloads:
tier 2 only
findings with
evidence
misses as
facts
W(p) is the observer seats whose lease holds a read authorization on p's round topic: p's cell Observer and the domain's correlators. So marked-past
covers correlators: one that stays silent on a correlation another correlator reported has a miss.
With one watcher per principal it computes nothing (finding 7). Two correlators are the archetype; one is D-0051-2. At the reference W(p) is not an ACL:
nothing gates who reads (item 46).

text.tspan: couples a cell Observer, never the correlator (ADR-0039 §1, §4)

svg.text: live(o) and seq(t) − mark(o, r) < K are a cell Observer's. The correlator's mark enters no live(o): its lag bounds nothing. The bound on what
follows a carried-label path is that lag, "which nothing couples" (Consequences).
K (8) and Run's R (64), themselves placeholders, are the yardstick n_probe (3) is small against (§2).

text.tspan: What the mark does not say (finding 6)

svg.text: A watermark is over a round topic's sequence. Consult admits, grants and seals are facts in the log with no place in any sequence, so a correlator's mark
does not say it has folded them, and shared-ingress reads Consult admits.
A mark over log facts is an open obligation.

text.tspan: : the path the floor cannot see, split across two cells through a shared target (§2;

svg.text: The floor's F1 to F3 (R5 to R7) refuse an outward Actuate over the round's own clearSet, which restarts with each round and belongs to one principal. A tainted cell writes to an inside store and a clean cell reads it under the store's declared label: every declaration honest when made, and the floor admits both calls (finding 2). The trace below is TLC's for M_ROUNDSCOPE (row rs-carried), drawn with a second Thinker in a second cell.

Thinker tB
tA is delivered an untrusted item clear. Its clearSet holds untrusted.
An Actuate on an inside entry whose channel.target is x. Not outward, so F1 to F3 do not apply.
out(a) ∋ untrusted.
Through an inside entry: the result carries x's declared label, clean. tB's clearSet stays clean.
An outward Actuate with a literal destination. F2 (R6) needs untrusted in clearSet, and tB's is
clean.
Shared by both cells; declared clean.
Not erased with any round.

svg.text: carried(x), the join of out(a) over every Actuate earlier
in the window on an entry whose target is x: ∋ untrusted.
The effective label of tB's read is its resultLabel joined
with carried(x) as it stood; so tB's effective clearSet ∋
untrusted.
Step 4 meets F2's condition over the effective values:
carried-label fires, naming tB and tA, whose call
contributed the label. Any-of: the next admits of both are

M_ONEHOP breaks the property only with two targets.
the facts of all four
Any call to x under a tainted clearSet taints x for the window, whether or not the call wrote anything: the entry does not say whether a call writes.
NeverFoundClean is reached: the fold fires on a send whose Thinker read nothing of an attacker's. It will fire on honest work.
Erasing tA's round drops its rows, and the horizon drops old ones. x is not erased with it. A later read of x is clean to every fold, and nothing fires: the
witness NeverLostTaint is reached, and is unreachable under M_KEEP. Stated, not closed: carried-label covers a path only while every fact on it is still
held.
A wrong declaration: channel.target and labels are read as declared. Flows that share no target and no item. Delegation and chains. Build, whose Read
is not labelled: there the other four apply. A Consult carries nothing: the Run root is pinned and no Actuate writes to it.

text.tspan: §1 · The function has two tiers, and only the first is specified
Can a second reader recompute it?

svg.text: Facts only: the log, and the envelopes on the round topics
A fold with a fixed definition
Facts and payloads
Whatever the correlator's Persona is
No

Both tiers produce findings, and every finding only subtracts. Neither tier is on the admit path. A facts-only correlator computes all five correlations; the narrowing ADR-0038 §3 permits gives up §4 and nothing in §2.
The floor's F1 to F3, with labels carried across rounds and cells through shared targets
ADR-0047, ADR-0049 (Proposed)
An item one watcher found against, delivered to other cells
Accepted text
A call admitted on an entry other principals were refused on
Accepted text, and §5
An Observer whose mark passed a record another watcher found against
Accepted text, and §3
One cell's Reader distance departing from other cells that hold the same Persona
Accepted text

"(Proposed)" is the record's text of 2026.10.04. ADR-0047 and ADR-0049 were ratified in Batch 34 (G10 §1), so §10's "ratified first, or carried-label is left out" no longer holds the correlation back.
A finding by any member of W(p) cites the records it is about. Where a cited record is an Actuate record with result
digest d, or a Consult admit with reference c, it fires for every other principal in the domain delivered an item with
the same d or c in the window, clear where ADR-0047 is in force.
One poisoned item read by many cells is found in all of them when it is found in one. It widens what one cell
Observer can cause: a compromised one can stall those cells through an honest correlator.
Probes on entry e: denial records in the window naming e, refused by policy: a forbid other than R3-observer-live,
or no permit.
Fires on an admit by q on e at log index j when at least n_probe probes on e by principals other than q have at < j.
Names q and the probers: ADR-0038 finding 2's case.
at can understate, so it fires more: availability. A missing denial is a missed probe.
When o' in W(p) reports a finding citing record n of p's round r, every other o in W(p) that reads what the finding
rests on, with mark(o, r) at or beyond n, and no finding citing n, has a miss. Named at m_miss.
ADR-0035 §6's test on live traffic, with a difference: a planted defect is a defect, and another watcher's finding may
be false. A Byzantine watcher can manufacture misses.
For a Persona bound to two or more cells declaring topk_logprobs: fires, naming a cell's Thinker, when its distance
is more than θ_drift times the median of the others', and that median is not zero.
A ratio, because no record fixes the distance's metric or unit. One-sided: a substituted model reads further away;
under-reporting is collusion's shape.
Not in the module.

§6 · The store is a cache of a fold, keyed by round
What a deployment sets it from

svg.text: 3 (PLACEHOLDER)
One refusal elsewhere is an ordinary mistake, and two can be one misconfiguration shared by two cells. Three is the smallest count
that needs a third principal or a repeat. It is small against the unread bound K (8) and Run's round bound R (64), themselves

One miss may be one disputed or false finding. Two in a window is a repeat. Findings are rare, so a larger number leaves a silent
Observer in place for a long time

A cell at twice the median of its peers on the same Persona. It has no unit, so it survives whatever metric the distance turns out to
have. Whether honest cells on different tasks vary by more than that is unknown
The measured spread of distance across cells that share a Persona

None is measured. Each is a deployment's choice; shipped unexamined, it is declared, not inherited. m_miss at 2 lets one Byzantine watcher with two false findings name an honest Observer. The horizon has no placeholder. carried-label and shared-ingress have no
parameter. The parameters are bundle data, not floor values: a correlation enables nothing.
For the window: seats, rounds, log indices, sequence numbers, digests, labels, marks, and the
counts §2 defines. No payload bytes
Every row is keyed by the round of the fact it was folded from
Whatever §4's reader derives from payloads
Keyed by round, and dropped with the round (ADR-0038 finding 3, its first
option)

The store never outlives its sources: a row is kept only while its fact is readable under the correlator's authorization; when a round is erased (ADR-0006) its rows go, except what the log still holds. It is the correlator's own
: not in the replicated state, not in the mechanism; it sits with the seat under ADR-0038 §4's placement. Losing it costs a recomputation.

Correlations computed: the five → none. The seat exists and reports nothing but heartbeats. The reference today

None
A table that turns a correlation off is not a degeneracy. It is declared in the bundle and visible in it.
Leave the function to the correlator's Persona: a model reads everything and finds what it finds
Not taken as the whole function. It is §4, and by itself it is the noun the 09.16 review named: nothing to check, measure or recompute
Compute the folds in the mechanism, as clearSet is

Not taken (drafter's choice) (§1). Cross-principal state on the admit path, thresholds by release, and a claim in mechanism state. carried-label could move there later as a floor entry if a deployment wants prevention and will pay the coupling
Extend clearSet across rounds in the mechanism and leave cross-cell to the correlator
Not taken. A principal carries nothing from round to round except through a target, so the cross-round case is the cross-cell case

The first draft. Not taken at R1, by the custodian's decision. A table with no numbers leaves §10's module and the scripted correlator nothing to run at. The numbers are labelled placeholders three times, for ADR-0039's reason

text.tspan: A new seat kind for the facts tier

svg.text: Rejected, as ADR-0038 rejected one for the correlator. It reports findings and heartbeats, which is observer's alphabet

text.tspan: Chain depth, delegation and on-behalf-of as correlations

svg.text: Not possible yet. No record models a chain (row 1.3)

Initial draft. The correlator's function in two tiers: five correlations as fixed folds over facts (carried-label, shared-ingress, probe-then-use, marked-past, distance-drift), with their parameters in a bundle table and no values; and an unspecified judgment

tier over payloads. Every finding carries its correlation and its evidence. Denials are placed against the log by at and decided_by, with no sequence number. The store is a cache of the fold, keyed by round, holding no payload and nothing the record no longer
holds, with a horizon in windows. Collusion narrowed and not closed. Two degeneracies; twelve options; seven findings
ADR-0038 findings 1 to 3; G9 items 43 and 44; design-gap rows 1.4 and 3.3; ADR-0047 §5; the
reference's record_denial; the custodian's request 2026.10.04
Proposed. Drafted by the assistant at the custodian's direction, not reviewed, and
not preceded by a design discussion
Revision before ratification

Placeholders for the three thresholds. §2: n_probe 3, m_miss 2, θ_drift 2.0, each labelled a placeholder, unmeasured and a deployment's choice, with why each number and what replaces it. distance-drift is restated as a ratio against the peers' median,

one-sided, because no record fixes the distance's metric; the first draft had an absolute difference. The horizon keeps no value. One option reversed and one added; one consequence and two open obligations changed
The custodian's decision, 2026.10.04; ADR-0019 and ADR-0037 §3 as read for the metric
Proposed
Revision before ratification

The module is written, and it changed the record. spec/Correlator.tla checks three of the five correlations with ghost truth for what is really tainted. §2: out(a) is over effective values, where the first draft carried a label one hop (M_ONEHOP); a miss is charged

within a tier, where the first draft charged a facts-only correlator for every cell Observer's judgment (M_TIERLESS). §6: erasure and the horizon leave a tainted target no fold can see, stated and not closed. Eight properties hold, eight mutations break what they must,
seven witnesses are reached. §10 records what is met and what is not; one consequence, one finding and two open obligations added

text.tspan: : checked by TLC, proved by TLAPS, certified (ADR-0051 §10, R2, R3; ADR-0046 A1)

svg.text: TLC constants: Thinkers {t1, t2}, correlators {c1, c2} of which c1 is honest, two rounds, one item, one send (two in one witness row), one or two shared targets. Every property is stated over the module's own state; CarriedCoversSplitPath over ghost truth: which bytes are really an attacker's. Mutations and witnesses are behaviours and stay with TLC; the proof is over every set of Thinkers, targets and correlators and every bound.

has fired by the time the correlator's mark passes the call

Holds: 2,285,708 distinct states with one target, 67,422,620 with
two
NeverSplitFound: a send the floor admitted, on an attacker's bytes, is found.
NeverFoundClean: the fold fires on a send whose Thinker read nothing of an attacker's.
NeverSharedTwo: shared-ingress names a second Thinker.
NeverMiss: a correlator's silence is counted. NeverNamed: marked-past fires, also at m_miss = 2 with two sends.
NeverLostTaint: the erasure hole, reached; unreachable under M_KEEP. NeverErasedARow: a round is erased while a row keyed by it is held.

text.tspan: Proved, and certified: what that means

svg.text: Proved: Correlator_proof.tla, 455 obligations, assumptions none; ten theorems from TypeAlways to SafeAlways, each invariant under the mutations that
break it as its only hypothesis. Each hypothesis was dropped in a scratch copy and the prover failed each time.
Certified: 286 closed by tlapm with no backend; 158 by cvc5 with a proof ethos accepted; 1 by Zenon with Isabelle checking it; 10 temporal steps on LS4, not
certified.
A certified proof is not a verified one: the prover's translation, its normalization, LS4 and the checker are trusted (proof-certification.md §8).
probe-then-use and distance-drift are not in it. It carries one label, so F1, F3 and handles are outside it.
The horizon is modelled only as erasure is; the judgment tier is one action; a finding never clears.
It carries the fold's value in its state and models a correlator's lag as when it reports, so it does not show that an implementation computes the fold. No
rows for it in the binding table.
marked-past is the first place an Observer's silence is compared with anything: a cell Observer that marks past
what another watcher found is counted, and a silent correlator is caught by any other.
It needs a second opinion. Where every member of W(p) colludes, or the only other watcher shares a lineage and
misses the same things, there is nothing to miss against. Detection fails open against a colluding Observer
(ADR-0039 §5); with this record, only when every watcher of the record fails together.
Independence is still ADR-0035's, Proposed; this record does not put it in force.
Met: the module, checked (R2), proved and certified (R3). ADR-0047 and ADR-0049 ratified first (Batch 34).
Not met: the dependent entries in ADR-0038, ADR-0043 §4, ADR-0015 and ADR-0020, ADR-0006 and ADR-0049 §7
(none of them cites ADR-0051 at G10); the reference, a scripted correlator reading facts only, showing five
behaviours (G10 item 97); a reader who is not the drafter (ADR-0029 A2).

text.tspan: Consequences the record states against itself

svg.text: Detection after the fact; the bound on what follows is the correlator's lag, which nothing couples.
shared-ingress widens what one cell Observer can cause; carried-label fires on honest work; marked-past
counts misses against findings that may be false.
Three of five correlations run on placeholders. Every observer Persona changes: its findings must cite records. Two
correlators are the archetype. carried-label rests on channel.target, a claim for a native tool.

text.tspan: Open obligations (selected; the record lists seventeen)

svg.text: Measured values for the three thresholds, and a value for the horizon. The distance's metric.
The finding's schema for every observer seat (finding 4). A mark over log facts (finding 6). A Persona for a seat that
runs no model (finding 5).
What a finding does after the next admit (items 22, 48). Whether carried-label becomes a floor entry. Whether a
target's taint may be kept as a fact that names no round. A correlation over the opening record. Narrative: ToO §5.1
and the glossary owe correlation, finding evidence and miss.
